# ethereum-optimism/infra Monthly Report (April 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In April 2026, development focused heavily on hardening the `proxyd` service and improving the reliability of the Superchain's interoperability layer. Significant progress was made in `proxyd` through a series of refactors and the introduction of consensus state tracking for safe and finalized block hashes. The team also successfully resolved several critical data consistency issues in `op-supernode` related to L1 reorg handling by implementing Write-Ahead Logging (WAL). Despite these advancements, the month was characterized by an intensive effort to triage a surge of flaky tests in the CI pipeline, particularly concerning flashblocks and unsafe gap filling.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### `proxyd` Service Enhancements & Refactoring
The `proxyd` service underwent significant architectural improvements to enhance its interaction with the Execution Layer (EL) and improve code maintainability.
*   **Consensus State Tracking:** Introduced tracking for `safeBlockHash` and `finalizedBlockHash`, ensuring block hashes previously discarded are now stored for more accurate fetching ([#591](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/591)).
*   **Architectural Refactoring:** Generic functions were renamed to EL-specific scopes to prevent type assertion panics ([#592](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/592)). A new `updateELBackend` function was extracted to encapsulate block fetches and validation ([#595](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/595)), and a reusable walk-back function for consensus block discovery was implemented ([#590](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/590)).
*   **New Architecture:** Initial work began on a new CL consensus architecture for `proxyd` ([#596](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/596), [#597](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/597)).

### Infrastructure & Dependency Management
*   **Observability Updates:** A suite of updates was applied to `op-acceptor`, bumping OpenTelemetry SDK and exporter dependencies from version 1.34.0 to 1.43.0 to maintain modern tracing standards ([#599](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/599), [#600](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/600), [#601](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/601)).
*   **Security & Maintenance:** The `replica-healthcheck` tool received a `lodash` dependency bump to address potential vulnerabilities and maintain upstream compatibility ([#598](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/598)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **L1 Reorg Consistency:** A major milestone was reached in `op-supernode` where issues regarding data pruning during L1 reorgs—including verifications, denied blocks, and the interop database—were resolved via WAL implementation ([#19245](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19245), [#19287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19287), [#19289](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19289)).
*   **Protocol Logic & Testing:** The Superroot SLA definition was finalized ([#19180](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19180)), and several acceptance tests for invalid executing messages were unskipped after successful validation ([#19712](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19712)).
*   **Challenger Updates:** Fixed host arguments in the Kona super executor to ensure `op-challenger` correctly runs interop tests ([#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18287)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **CI Stability (Flaky Tests):** A significant portion of the month's triage was dedicated to recurring test failures. `TestFlashblocksStream` ([#19883](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19883)) and `TestFlashblocksTransfer` ([#19934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19934)) are showing timing races and "address already in use" errors. `TestSuperchain` was also reopened due to suspected panics in the Sepolia subtest ([#19586](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19586)).
*   **Runtime Configuration:** A new high-priority issue was opened to implement reactive runtime config reloads for `op-node`. This aims to prevent verifier nodes from rejecting valid blocks during signer rotations ([#19981](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19981)).
*   **Derivation & Resource Leaks:** Potential resource leaks were identified in `op-node/p2p` regarding gossip topics not closing on shutdown ([#19860](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19860)), alongside logic errors in `op-batcher` regarding L1 origin comparisons ([#19859](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19859)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month showed strong internal technical coordination, particularly between contributors `wwared`, `maurelian`, and `sebastianst` in diagnosing complex race conditions within the CI environment. There is an ongoing strategic shift in testing infrastructure, as evidenced by the migration of `op-e2e` interop action tests to the `op-acceptance-tests` suite ([#18974](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18974)). Discussions around interop transaction pool eviction behavior ([#19351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19351)) highlight a collaborative effort to balance implementation simplicity in `op-reth` with the safety requirements of the Superchain.
